name: devices.list
description: List this device and directly connected devices with runtime, version, implemented tools, automation switch and actual automation-channel state. Use target="local". Discovery does not verify or grant permissions; missing legacy capabilities are null.

supportedTools.description: Implemented tool names, independent of the current automation switch and caller permissions. Null means unknown.

name: sessions.list
description: Inspect active streams and connection state on the explicit target. localTracks.id is a trackId for screen.configure and the existing-stream form of control.acquire. captureSourceId is the screen.sources capture ID; sourceId is an internal publication ID, not a capture ID. To prepare a monitor and acquire control together, pass a monitor capture ID directly to control.acquire.sourceId.

id.description: Stream track ID; choose state=live for operations and pass as trackId, never as a capture sourceId.

sourceId.description: Internal publication ID; not accepted as a native capture source ID.

name: screen.sources
description: List native monitor and window capture sources and available physical display geometry. For desktop control, choose sources[].kind=monitor and pass its id as sourceId to control.acquire; sharing is prepared automatically. For a screenshot, pass a monitor or window id to control.screenshot. Source discovery does not start sharing or acquire control.

name: screen.start
description: Start or reuse a room-wide screen share without acquiring control. For desktop input, prefer control.acquire with a monitor sourceId. sourceId is a capture ID from screen.sources. Returns trackId and reused. New shares have audio off; reused shares preserve audio and settings. Successful sharing persists after control release, caller disconnection or permission expiry. Reuse never transfers close permission. Only the original requester can screen.stop a requested picture, while nobody else controls it; a picture shared manually by the host can only be closed by the host.

sourceId.description: Monitor or window capture ID from screen.sources.sources[].id.

reused.description: True if an existing live screen publication was reused. Older targets may omit this field.

name: screen.stop
description: Close a room-wide picture originally opened by this caller through screen.start or control.acquire(sourceId), using its trackId. Stops audio and control transport for all viewers. Host-shared pictures and pictures opened by another caller return PERMISSION_DENIED; reuse and control handoff never transfer close permission. Returns CONTROL_BUSY while another caller controls this picture; retry after they release control. After reconnecting, the original caller must claim its existing source again with screen.start. Use control.release to end input while keeping the picture. released/stopped confirm closure; legacy targets may return retained=true.

name: screen.configure
description: Update a running stream using trackId returned by control.acquire, screen.start or sessions.list.localTracks[].id. Supply all video limits; this changes the current stream, not persistent preferences. sourceId capture IDs and publication IDs are not track IDs. Use screen.settings.update for saved preferences.

name: screen.settings.get
description: Read saved desktop video sharing preferences and available encoders, codecs, presets and capture backends. These are preferences, not the effective settings of a running stream; use diagnostics for those. Requires automation on the target.

name: screen.settings.update
description: Update a nonempty subset of saved desktop video preferences. Read screen.settings.get first for supported choices. Encoder and codec must form a supported pair (automatic selection requires both encoder and codec to be auto); preset is remembered for the selected encoder. Resolution, frameRate, maxBitrate and degradationPreference request asynchronous live updates through the app; other fields apply on the next share. Returns previous/settings and changed fields grouped by application timing, not confirmation of live success. Does not restart sharing. Requires automation on the target.

name: control.acquire
description: Acquire desktop control with a monitor sourceId from screen.sources; sharing starts or is reused automatically. Alternatively pass trackId for an already live native monitor. Supply exactly one ID. sourceId requires screen.manage and input.control; new shares have audio off and reused shares retain settings. Returns trackId for screen.configure, plus sourceId, bounds and geometryRevision for pointer input. shareReused describes screen reuse and is present only for sourceId calls; reused describes borrowing the same device's manual control grant. Call control.pointer/key/text directly, then control.release to end input while keeping the picture. Sharing persists after caller disconnection. Reuse and control handoff never transfer close permission; screen.stop only closes a picture opened by this caller while nobody else controls it. Repeated acquisition preserves the lease and optional window binding; an exclusive owner can switch monitors. Failure releases the unused temporary share.

trackId.description: Existing live native monitor track ID from sessions.list.localTracks[].id or screen.start. Does not start or retain a new screen share. Mutually exclusive with sourceId.

sourceId.description: Capture ID of a kind=monitor entry in screen.sources.sources[]. Prepares sharing and control in one call. Mutually exclusive with trackId; do not pass a publication ID.
Native monitor capture ID for control.pointer and control.screenshot; not a publication ID.

reused.description: Whether this lease borrows the same verified device's manual control grant; does not describe screen reuse.

trackId.description: Acquired live stream track ID for screen.configure. Older targets may omit this field.

shareReused.description: Whether sourceId acquisition reused an existing screen publication. Omitted for trackId calls and older targets; independent of reused.

name: control.bindWindow
description: Optional window confinement; omit this tool for normal desktop input. Bind keyboard, text and pointer input to a top-level windowId returned as elementId by accessibility.windows. Requires acquired control and all keys/buttons released. Attempts foreground activation once; subsequent focus loss/window destruction stops input. Loss of the bound window during an action is reported as WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST, including closure. The action may already have taken effect; inspect windows or a screenshot before retrying. Pointer points must belong to the visible bound window and acquired monitor. Bind once per control lease; release/acquire to change or remove binding. UIA semantic actions retain their explicit element targets.

name: control.release
description: Release this caller's input lease and held inputs while keeping shared pictures. Sharing created by either screen.start or control.acquire persists after control release or caller disconnection. Use screen.stop to explicitly close the room-wide picture. A borrowed manual control grant remains active.

name: control.screenshot
description: Capture a monitor or window as a losslessly compressed PNG using sourceId from screen.sources (not a UIA elementId). Fits within maxWidth/maxHeight (default 1024 each, maximum 2048), preserving aspect ratio without upscaling. Use window or rect crops for fine details. Optional rect {left,top,width,height} uses absolute desktopPhysicalPixels and must be wholly inside the selected source; crop happens before scaling. Returns cropped physical bounds, actual image dimensions, geometryRevision and imageToDesktop. Map image points back to desktop coordinates for control.pointer; never apply DPI scale again. Refresh after display/window movement. PNG is limited to 4 MiB; use a smaller region or size on RESULT_TOO_LARGE.

sourceId.description: Monitor or window sourceId returned by screen.sources.

rect.description: Crop in absolute desktop physical pixels before resizing; must lie wholly inside the selected monitor or window.

name: control.pointer
description: Mouse actions in desktopPhysicalPixels, bound to sourceId and geometryRevision from control.acquire. No window binding or focus call is required for desktop input; click directly at screen coordinates. An optional bindWindow confines input to that window. action is required: move jumps to x/y, or follows path from x/y; drag presses at x/y, follows path then releases. path has 1..128 waypoints; durationMs defaults to 500 (16..10000). down/up maintain button state across calls, with a 30-second hold limit. click supports clickCount 1..2, holdMs (default 30) and intervalMs (default 100). scroll requires scrollX and scrollY (120 units per detent, use 0 for the unused axis). Input actions execute serially. Cancellation, stale geometry or lost authority releases the affected control lease.

name: control.key
description: Send named physical keys to the current foreground application using the acquired control lease; no bindWindow or focus call is required. An optional bindWindow confines input to that window. Actions: press, down, up or ordered chord (reverse release). Timed actions default to holdMs=30, repeat=1, intervalMs=100; total scheduled duration <=10 seconds. Names are physical positions, not text. Held keys can combine with mouse actions; overlapping presses are rejected.

name: control.text
description: Type committed Unicode text into the current foreground application's focused control using the acquired control lease; no bindWindow or focus call is required. An optional bindWindow confines input to that window. Controls (including newline/Tab) require control.key. All held keys/buttons must first be released. Cancellable chunks preserve Unicode characters; intervalMs optionally spaces characters, with <=10 seconds of scheduled gaps.

name: accessibility.capabilities
description: Read desktop accessibility backend availability, supported semantic actions, bounded state/value inspection and limits. Capability discovery does not grant permission.

name: accessibility.windows
description: List accessible top-level windows with opaque element references valid for up to 60 seconds. Excludes Weblink itself. Window names are sensitive.

nameTruncated.description: Present and true when name was truncated; truncated names never satisfy exact-name wait conditions.

name: accessibility.snapshot
description: Read a bounded, flat accessibility subtree from an elementId, including supported toggle/selection/expansion states. includeValues=true opts into bounded Value/Text pattern content; maxTextLength defaults to 1024 and is capped at 4096 characters per value/text. Password controls remain redacted. truncated means more nodes exist.

nameTruncated.description: Present and true when name was truncated; truncated names never satisfy exact-name wait conditions.

name: accessibility.action
description: Perform a supported semantic action on an elementId. Requires control.acquire and its active exclusive input lease. setValue requires value (empty clears); other actions forbid value. All prior caller references expire after dispatch. Optional observeAfter returns fresh references from its elementId (defaults to the acted element), using valid independent accessibility.read permission. A successful observation sets refreshRequired=false; otherwise refreshRequired=true. An applied action followed by a failed observation returns applied=true with observationError; do not repeat the action to recover an observation. No keyboard fallback.

nameTruncated.description: Present and true when name was truncated; truncated names never satisfy exact-name wait conditions.

name: accessibility.wait
description: Wait for AND-matched conditions on the same existing element identity using UIA events, without clicking or reselecting by label. Read the current state once, then re-read only after an event notification; there is no periodic polling or final scan at the deadline. Conditions inspect enabled/focused/offscreen/selection/toggle/expansion states, exact exposed name/value, or bounded textContains. Value/Text are read only when requested by a text condition; protected controls remain excluded. The only timing option is timeoutMs: an overall timeout of 5000 by default, range 1-30000. Returns matched, timedOut, elapsedMs and a fresh node reference on a match, or node:null on timeout. Missing provider events can cause a timeout even if the condition changed; callers may explicitly take a new snapshot to investigate. A timeout does not prove a prior action failed. Stale references and lost permission require a new observation/authorization.

nameTruncated.description: True when the full name was truncated; it cannot satisfy an exact-name condition.

name: commands.capabilities
description: Read the target device's command backend capabilities without starting a job. Returns supported, transport (pipe or none), stdin, eof, pty, supportedSignals and signalSemantics. Windows pipe jobs support SIGTERM/SIGKILL (both terminate the process tree); Unix supports SIGINT/SIGTERM (process-group signals) and SIGKILL (terminate the process tree). Query the actual target before commands.send; the controller's OS does not determine remote support. Browser-local queries return supported=false and no signals. Capability discovery does not grant shell.execute permission or guarantee that a shell executable is installed.

name: commands.run
description: Run a pipe-based shell command (no PTY) and wait up to waitMs (default 10000, maximum 60000). Returns jobId, status, exitCode and the latest 16384 output bytes (chunks/startCursor/nextCursor), prioritizing final results/errors. If still running, background=true; continue commands.read with nextCursor. Use commands.read(cursor=0) for retained earlier output. timeoutMs independently limits process lifetime. Cancelling the call before handoff cancels the job. Up to 10 concurrent jobs per device. Stdin stays open; commands.send writes UTF-8 input, closes stdin (eof), or sends a signal.

name: commands.start
description: Start a pipe-based shell job (no PTY) in the background and return jobId immediately. Use commands.read(target,jobId) for the latest 16384 bytes, or tailLines/tailBytes for a smaller tail. Follow new output by passing nextCursor as cursor; poll until status is not running and hasMore=false. timeoutMs defaults to 60000, maximum 600000. stdout/stderr share one absolute byte cursor. Oldest output is evicted to retain the latest 4 MiB/8192 stream segments. Up to 10 concurrent jobs per device. Stdin stays open; commands.send writes UTF-8 input, closes stdin (eof), or sends a signal.

name: commands.status
description: Read job status (running/completed/cancelled/timed_out), exitCode, cumulative bytes, retainedBytes, earliestCursor, truncated (old output evicted), and outputIncomplete (pipe read failed or draining timed out). Does not return output; use commands.read for the latest output or incremental reads. stdinStatus is open, closing (EOF queued), closed, or failed (pipe write failed).

name: commands.read
description: Read the latest 16384 output bytes by default. Select only one of: tailBytes (1-16384), tailLines (1-1000 LF-delimited lines, still capped at 16384 bytes; tailLimited marks this cap), or cursor (absolute byte offset for incremental reads; 0 requests earliest retained output). Returns stdout/stderr chunks with display data and exact dataBase64, startCursor, nextCursor, hasMore, status, exitCode, cumulative bytes, retainedBytes, earliestCursor, truncated, cursorExpired, tailLimited and outputIncomplete (pipe read failed or draining timed out). Retain latest 4 MiB/8192 stream segments; old output is evicted. An expired cursor resumes at earliestCursor with cursorExpired=true. Follow with nextCursor; hasMore=false means caught up now, keep polling while running. Access requires the original caller and shell grant. stdinStatus is open, closing (EOF queued), closed, or failed (pipe write failed).

name: commands.send
description: Send to your running job: UTF-8 input (literal text, no implicit newline), optional eof=true to close stdin after queued input, or a signal (exclusive with input/eof). Returns queued=true when accepted, not an acknowledgement that the process consumed it. Input is limited to 16384 characters/65536 UTF-8 bytes per call and 8 queued messages; BUSY means nothing was queued. After EOF, input is rejected. SIGKILL cancels the process tree on all platforms; SIGTERM sends POSIX TERM on Unix and terminates the process tree on Windows. SIGINT sends POSIX INT on Unix; Windows returns UNSUPPORTED_SIGNAL (no console/PTY). Signals bypass blocked stdin. Use commands.read/status to observe output, stdinStatus and completion. Requires the original caller and shell grant.

name: diagnostics.snapshot
description: Read latest redacted stream statistics and sample availability.

name: diagnostics.history
description: Read up to 30 samples after a cursor from the last five minutes.

name: diagnostics.start
description: Start a bounded detailed diagnostic capture without screen contents.

name: diagnostics.stop
description: Stop the detailed diagnostic capture.

name: diagnostics.export
description: Export a paginated redacted diagnostic report; no SDP, IPs, credentials or screen contents.
